    Control of push-down constructions on total spaces #

    Propositions 4.4, 4.7 and 4.8, for maps between the total spaces ⊕_i L(T)(i) satisfying the block equations of a push-down along a quiver morphism p : D → Q injective on the arrows with a fixed source and on those with a fixed target. Here L : D → Rep D is fully faithful and a morphism φ : T → U with T ∈ C whose image L(φ) vanishes at one vertex is zero (ZeroAtVertex, Lemmas 2.2(1) and 4.2). The positions (j, i) of blocks are partitioned into classes (BlockClasses): components of the matching quiver for walks, elements of the group for coverings. The classes are closed under the edges of the matching quiver, the diagonal is a union of classes, and on each class off the diagonal the second coordinate determines the first and some column is missing.

    • bl_self_eq_zero: a map p_*L(T) → p_*L(U), T ∈ C, with a zero column has zero diagonal blocks.
    • bl_comp_self: the diagonal part is multiplicative.
    • eq_zero_of_mem_closure_good: a composite of |D₀| maps with zero diagonal parts vanishes (the argument of Lemma 4.3).

          Chains of maps with zero diagonal part (the argument of Lemma 4.3) #

          The nilpotence argument only needs a family of representations Xf o of D, a notion of admissible column Adm o c, the vanishing of the diagonal blocks of a map with a zero admissible column (DiagZero), and an admissible zero column for each piece of a map (ColAdm).
